facts.heading: GP suggested visit due to exhaustion
facts.content: Daniel's general practitioner suggested he come to therapy because she observed he looked exhausted.
facts.evidence: My general practitioner suggested I come. She said I look exhausted

facts.heading: Burnout started in October
facts.content: Daniel has been completely burnt out since October.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burnt out since October

facts.heading: Workload increased after client loss
facts.content: Daniel's team lost a big client in October.
facts.evidence: We lost a big client

facts.heading: Daniel took on extra work
facts.content: Daniel ended up doing three people's jobs after the client loss.
facts.evidence: so I ended up doing three people's jobs

facts.heading: Works late and thinks about work
facts.content: Daniel starts work at 7 am and continues answering messages until 10 pm.
facts.evidence: I'm at my desk by 7 and I'm still answering messages at 10 that night

facts.heading: Sleep is poor, wakes at 3 am
facts.content: Daniel sleeps about 4 hours most nights.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about 4 hours

facts.heading: Wakes at 3 am with worry
facts.content: When Daniel wakes at 3 am, he experiences a headache and worries about shipping schedules and clients.
facts.evidence: My head just hurts. Shipping schedules, the client

facts.heading: Father diagnosed with Parkinson's
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
facts.evidence: my father. He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn

facts.heading: Daniel drives father to hospital
facts.content: Daniel drives his father to the hospital in Leeds for neurology appointments every few weeks.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds

facts.heading: Daniel is primary caregiver
facts.content: Daniel is the one handling the care for his father because his sister Hannah lives in Toronto.
facts.evidence: all the care for our father falls of me

facts.heading: Daniel feels guilty about fatigue
facts.content: Daniel feels guilty for being tired when his father is ill.
facts.evidence: He feels selfish to be tired when he's the one who's ill

facts.heading: Girlfriend Claire noticed his state
facts.content: Claire, Daniel's girlfriend, booked the appointment because she was tired of seeing him disappear.
facts.evidence: Claire. She said she was done watching me disappear

facts.heading: Daniel avoids weekend trips
facts.content: Daniel has been saying no to weekend trips suggested by Claire.
facts.evidence: I always said no

facts.heading: Work emails prevent rest
facts.content: Daniel feels that if he takes time off, he will return to 200 emails.
facts.evidence: I'll come back to 200 of them

facts.heading: Stopped running two months ago
facts.content: Daniel stopped running about two months ago because his legs felt like lead.
facts.evidence: I stopped about two months ago. My legs feel like lead

facts.heading: Boss sends late emails
facts.content: Daniel's boss, Peterson, sends emails at 11 pm and expects answers before breakfast.
facts.evidence: he sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast

facts.heading: Daniel answers boss's late emails
facts.content: Daniel answers every email from his boss, even if he is not well.
facts.evidence: I answer it. Every time

facts.heading: Fear of job loss due to restructuring
facts.content: Daniel is worried about being let go due to a restructuring happening this spring.
facts.evidence: There's a restructuring this spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.

facts.heading: Financial responsibility
facts.content: Daniel has a mortgage.
facts.evidence: I have a mortgage.

facts.heading: Symptoms of anxiety/panic attacks
facts.content: Daniel experiences flat mood and irritability. He had an episode where his heart was racing and hands were shaking in the toilets.
facts.evidence: Flat, mostly. And irritable.

facts.heading: Past panic attack on train
facts.content: Daniel experienced a similar episode once on a train to Manchester.
facts.evidence: Once on a train to Manchester, just to get off and stand on a platform.

facts.heading: Fear of losing control
facts.content: Daniel fears that the symptoms mean he is losing his mind or going to end up 'coping'.
facts.evidence: That I'm losing it. That I'm going to end up, like, I don't know, coping.

facts.heading: Substance use for coping
facts.content: Daniel drinks about six cups of coffee daily. He has started having two to three glasses of wine in the evenings to 'switch his head off'.
facts.evidence: Coffee, probably. I want about six cups a day. And I've started having wine in the evenings to switch my head off. Two glasses, sometimes three.

facts.heading: Sleep difficulties
facts.content: Daniel wakes up at three in the morning.
facts.evidence: I wake at three anyway.

facts.heading: Relief from sharing burdens
facts.content: Daniel felt a sense of relief after sharing what he was carrying.
facts.evidence: A bit of relief actually. Like putting it on bad, but I didn't realize I was carrying.

facts.heading: Primary need is sleep
facts.content: Daniel believes that if he could sleep, he could cope with other issues.
facts.evidence: The nights, I think. If I could sleep, I could probably cope with the rest.

facts.heading: Family influence on stoicism
facts.content: Daniel's grandfather worked in the mines in Yorkshire and never complained.
facts.evidence: My grandfather worked at the mines in Yorkshire. He never complained about anything. Not once.

facts.heading: Belief about appearing weak
facts.content: Daniel fears his grandfather would think he was weak for being in therapy/struggling.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here.

facts.heading: Agreed to small behavioral change
facts.content: Daniel agreed to try setting aside 20 minutes in the evening to switch off his phone.
facts.evidence: Yeah, half past nine perhaps. I could make it a dangles glare.

facts.heading: Plan to track sleep
facts.content: Daniel agreed to note how his night goes when he wakes up.
facts.evidence: I can do that. Right down when I wake up. If I wake up.

facts.heading: Current feeling after session
facts.content: Daniel feels tired but lighter after the session.
facts.evidence: Tired, but lighter.
